title: Why Your Friend Quits After Their First Game

scenes.title: 첫 한 판을 지키는 설계
lines: The kart rounds a corner and continues down the track. This is routine for an experienced player. For a newcomer, keeping the race going can already be a small success. We will examine opponents’ intentions and assistance with the first controls, then look at when to step back.

Being kind to beginners does not mean winning for them. It means protecting their chance to try and recognize the result, so they can want another attempt. The difference is clearest in a first match against someone else.

scenes.title: 상대의 목적은 화면에 없다
lines: Imagine arcade fighting cabinets from years ago. The screens face away from each other, hiding the person at the other controls. A challenger joins, and the expert uses jumping attacks and special moves in succession. Skill is visible on screen, but the challenger’s expectations are not.

In a fighting game, reducing the opponent’s health wins the round. Successful attacks and a shrinking health bar are good results under the rules. For a first-time player, however, this may be repeated hits without understanding when to defend.

One person may expect a serious contest, while the other has merely tried a machine for fun with a friend. They share a match but have different intentions. When an opponent cannot respond, read that situation before displaying another technique.

scenes.title: 전력 승부에도 전제가 있다
lines: Automatically letting the other person win can also miss the point. If an opponent explicitly wants your best, they may dislike being patronized. The etiquette of an all-out match assumes that both people want it.

When playing together for the first time, agree on the immediate goal. It might be learning movement and defense, blocking a particular attack, or jumping straight into a match. Leaving an achievable action gives even a loss something to teach.

For example, explain the guard input, then demonstrate one recognizable attack. After blocking it, the newcomer can choose the next action. A visible result becomes connected to their own input. That care can also be built into a game’s opening experience.

scenes.title: 첫 조작에서 재미까지
lines: A new player still has many unknowns. The buttons and screen indicators are unfamiliar, along with what to do right now. Onboarding eases that burden between first contact and a first taste of the fun.

This matters in competitive and single-player games alike. If fun begins only after every control has been memorized, people may leave before reaching it. Let them try one action first, show its result, then add the next action.

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe combines acceleration, steering, and items in a race. Following a corner may already occupy a newcomer’s attention. Several simultaneous inputs leave less room to understand the race. Some of that burden can be selectively reduced.

scenes.title: 보조는 선택을 남긴다
lines: Smart Steering helps steer when the kart is about to leave the course around a corner. Enabling it adds an antenna to the back of the kart. Auto-Accelerate keeps it moving without holding the acceleration button. These options handle different burdens.

Reducing the need to hold acceleration leaves more attention for corners and items. Steering assistance lets someone begin by developing a feel for the track. Rather than removing every action, it creates room to focus on what they are learning.

The player can turn assistance off as they become comfortable. While Smart Steering is enabled, the third drift-boost stage, Ultra Mini-Turbo, is unavailable. The design widens the entrance while leaving room to learn more precise control.

scenes.title: 입력을 덜어도 판단은 남는다
lines: Fighting games show the same principle. Street Fighter 6’s Dynamic controls choose attacks after button inputs using circumstances such as distance. At close range and at long range, the same input can produce different actions.

Dynamic controls are available offline in certain Fighting Ground modes. They do not automate all online matches. For someone blocked by complex commands, they offer an early experience of attack range and combat flow.

Separate what assistance handles from what the player still decides. When one input burden is reduced, does it open room for a judgment they could not previously make? If the helper takes every judgment away as well, another problem appears.

scenes.title: 끌고 가면 발견이 사라진다
lines: Constant instructions about the next button, path, and action may reduce mistakes. They also reduce opportunities to choose. A helpful beginning can become carrying out another person’s sequence.

In A Short Hike, a small bird walks around an island, climbs surfaces, and glides from heights. Following an uphill path can lead to gliding toward a place that catches the eye. Choosing where to go within the visible landscape, then moving and seeing the result, is part of exploration’s pleasure.

Announcing every shortcut and destination in advance takes away the feeling of discovery. Explain controls and rules when needed, and leave space for the person to choose the next action. Knowing when to step back matters alongside how much help to provide.

scenes.title: 작은 관심을 다음 한 판으로
lines: Getting someone interested enough to try a game is already difficult. That small opening need not be extinguished by a one-sided match or relentless instructions. Help the first willingness to try become another attempt.

Agree on the kind of contest, share the burden of the first controls, and return decisions as confidence grows. The newcomer can then reach for another try by choice, because of a result they discovered themselves.
People play games to enjoy themselves. Open a path that lets someone reach that enjoyment under their own power. Kindness to beginners protects their choice to play the next game.
